text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — segfault spike in runtime-prod (gpu-pool-3). Paging @oncall-sre and @oncall-ml — error rate increased 18% over baseline, 60% of model-serving pods restarting.

alice: noticing lots of 502s from hosted API, saw crashloop restarts on several nodes, probably related to the quantized kernel roll last night.

dmitri: can someone paste the last lines from one of the pod logs? grabbing kubectl now.

bob: `kubectl -n inference logs runtime-pod-7 -c runtime | tail -n 50` output:```
runtime.so(+0x12af3)
runtime_trt_kernel.so(+0x4b2a)
SIGSEGV: segmentation fault at address 0x7ffdeadbeef
Backtrace (most recent call first):
  0x55a1f7c1 runtime::Dispatch()
  0x55a1f9d0 trt::runKernel()
  0x7f3b2c0 python3.10
```

carla: stack looks like a native crash inside our TensorRT fused kernel. we rolled a quantization change yesterday (image tag v2.4.0-quant).

oncall-sre: ack, taking initial lead. tagging @ops-bridge to open bridge and capture metrics.

ops-bridge: bridge created -> https://zoom.company/ops-bridge-1945501234. capturing node-level metrics and gpu mem stats.

alice: repro steps: send long-chat sequences (>=4096 tokens) to model-x-quant and pods die after ~2k tokens generated. short requests are fine.

dmitri: this smells like a KV cache or sequence-length edge case in the fused kernels. likely a pointer arithmetic bug triggered by the quant path.

oncall-ml: suggested quick mitigations: 1) rollback image to v2.3.9 (pre-quant) 2) add node selector to avoid gpu-pool-3 3) disable fused-kernel via env `USE_FUSED_KERNEL=0` in deployment.

oncall-sre: doing quick canary rollback to v2.3.9 on 2 pods now, will monitor.

bob: command used: `kubectl -n inference set image deploy/runtime runtime=registry.redwood/runtime:v2.3.9 --record`

alice: FYI the hosted customers impacted: 7 customers with heavy chat endpoints, ~1.2k failed requests in last 10m. support alerted.

carla: adding temporary rate-limiter and lowering max_req_tokens for model-x to 2048 to reduce exposure while we fix.

oncall-sre: canary rollback complete on pods runtime-pod-2/5. health checks green after 45s. crash count for those pods -> 0. overall error-rate down to +6% (was +18%).

dmitri: good, please keep a few quant-pods up for deeper debugging. I’ll attach gdb and get a native stack with symbols.

oncall-ml: taking over incident for deeper triage (handing off from SRE). marking in channel: @oncall-ml is now primary. @oncall-sre stay on standby for rollback if needed.

oncall-ml: notes for follow-up: reproduce with instrumented build, collect core dumps (enable `ulimit -c unlimited`), add additional bounds checks to trt loader, run valgrind/ASAN in CI for quant path.

ops-bridge: customer impact summary for postmortem: 7 customers, 1.2k failed requests, median extra-latency for degraded pods ~420ms, no data exfiltration.

oncall-sre: will keep alert until full fleet is stable. next steps: postmortem doc, priority fix for quant fused-kernel, and a hotpatch release plan.

alice: thanks — oncall-ml, ping me if you need more logs or to coordinate with support for customer comms.

oncall-ml: will do. scheduling follow-up runbook and assigning owners. marking incident as mitigated for now — error-rate returned close to baseline after rollback/cfg changes. will follow up with full RCA.

incident-bot: Incident state update: mitigated -> monitoring. Created postmortem draft at https://docs.company/incidents/1945501234-quant-kernel-segv.

carla: added a quick note: do NOT deploy v2.4.0-quant to prod until fix validated. moving the PR with address sanitizer to top of queue. :thumbsup:

oncall-ml: handing back to oncall-sre for final runbook items and closure. oncall-sre: please close when verified.

oncall-sre: will verify for 2 hours then close. thanks everyone.
